acceptance_results.evidence: git status and git diff in the seeded run directory show no change after the run; the memo's own scope statement records no code changes.

All three named risks handled concretely: revocation anchored to an explicit invariant (no decision started after a revocation ACK may allow that credential) with the state change and its audit event in one transaction/outbox, subject_epoch collapsing role-revoke and session-revoke, and honest limits stated for already-started requests; drift bounded by same-input/same-version shadow comparison with a five-way mismatch classification and checksum/revision watermarks gating state-ownership transfer; audit continuity via a caller-generated decision_id spanning local, remote, and business events, exactly one authoritative=true evaluator per decision, dedupe on decision_id + evaluator + mode, and periodic reconciliation of audit counts against routing logs.

Every behavior-changing stage is guarded: per action/tenant kill switches, cohorts fixed by tenant/action so engines never alternate per request, operator-explicit rollback gated on the legacy projection being verifiably current, automatic local fallback banned, and reverse replication required during the write-ownership rollback window — all preserving decision consistency under rollback.
